i18n.en: In that day YHWH will punish, with his hard and great and strong sword, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, and Leviathan the twisting serpent, and he will slay the dragon that is in the sea.
i18n.he: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ בְּחַרְב֨וֹ הַקָּשָׁ֜ה וְהַגְּדוֹלָ֣ה וְהַֽחֲזָקָ֗ה עַ֤ל לִוְיָתָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ בָּרִ֔חַ וְעַל֙ לִוְיָתָ֔ן נָחָ֖שׁ עֲקַלָּת֑וֹן וְהָרַ֥ג אֶת־הַתַּנִּ֖ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיָּֽם׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Liwyāṯān* (Leviathan) at 27:1 is the Hebrew Bible's clearest surviving **chaoskampf**, and the epithet-pair the verse hangs on it is among the most precise Ugaritic–Hebrew matches in the combat-myth corpus. YHWH, with his 'hard and great and strong sword' (*ḥereḇ qāšāh gᵉḏôlāh ḥăzāqāh*), 'punishes' (*yip̄qōḏ*, the *pqd* verb that returns protectively at 27:3) *liwyāṯān nāḥāš bāriaḥ* — 'Leviathan the fleeing serpent' — and *liwyāṯān nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn* — 'Leviathan the twisting serpent' — and slays *hat-tannîn ʾăšer bay-yām*, 'the dragon that is in the sea.' The translation keeps the plain surface: proper-noun 'Leviathan' (central `leviathan`), *bāriaḥ* 'fleeing' (over ASV 'swift', JPS 'slant'), *ʿăqallāṯôn* 'twisting' (over ASV 'crooked', JPS 'tortuous'), and *tannîn* 'the dragon' (the KJV/JPS dragon-register, over ASV 'monster'; central `taninim`).

The Ugaritic Baal Cycle names the same monster with the same two epithets. In ʿAnatu's victory-boast (KTU 1.3 III 40–42) and in Môtu's speech (KTU 1.5 I 1–3), Baʿlu's slain adversary is *ltn* (Lôtanu / Litan) — *bṯn brḥ* 'fleeing serpent' and *bṯn ʿqltn* 'twisting serpent', *šlyṭ d šbʿt rʾašm* 'tyrant with seven heads.' Hebrew *nāḥāš bāriaḥ / nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn* is the word-for-word cognate of Ugaritic *bṯn brḥ / bṯn ʿqltn*, and *liwyāṯān* is the cognate of *ltn* (both from proto-Semitic √lwy 'coil, wind'). J. Day (*God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea*, 1985) makes this the central case that the Hebrew Bible inherited a Northwest-Semitic combat-myth; D. Tsumura (*Creation and Destruction*, 2005) is the sober counter-voice, reading the Hebrew attestations as rhetorical-poetic redeployment of inherited imagery rather than a live cosmogonic combat. The translation commits to neither: the epithet-parallel is lexical fact, and the surface English carries no comparative freight (the cross-corpus governance is recorded in the central `lotanu-leviathan-…` and `chaoskampf-…` cluster entries, whose *appliesTo* now include this verse; the merely-locative *bay-yām* 'in the sea' here is the dragon's habitat, so the deified-Sea `yamm-…` entry is deliberately not applied).

> **Wheel of Heaven reading (interpretive layer, beyond the text).** Isaiah's eschatological sword falls on the same seven-headed serpent that Ugarit (Lôtanu), Babylon (Tiamat in *Enūma Eliš*), and the wider Indo-European dragon-cycles independently remember. Through the project's lens these convergent combat-myths are read as one node in a cross-cultural **Theomachy-convergence** — mythic compressions of remembered conflict among the Elohim. This synthesis goes beyond both the verse and the comparative philology; it is offered as the project's interpretive layer, not as the meaning of the Hebrew, and is flagged for human sign-off in the editor report.

i18n.en: In that day: a pleasant vineyard — sing of it!

notes.official: The vineyard-song of 27:2–6 is the deliberate redemptive **inversion** of the Song of the Vineyard at Isa 5:1–7. There YHWH's vineyard (Israel/Judah) yielded wild grapes and was stripped of its hedge, trampled, and laid waste; here YHWH is its keeper who waters it 'every moment' (27:3), disclaims wrath toward it (27:4), and it takes root and fills the world with fruit (27:6). The same *kerem* lexeme opens both songs (central `kerem-vineyard`, Gen-9:20-scoped, not extended here). The opening colon carries a text-critical variant: MT *kerem ḥemed* 'a pleasant vineyard / vineyard of delight' against 1QIsaᵃ (and the tradition behind ASV) *kerem ḥemer* 'a vineyard of wine' — a near-homograph ד/ר confusion. The translation retains MT *ḥemed* and discloses the scroll's *ḥemer* for audit; *ʿannû-lāh* is the antiphonal 'sing of it,' the feminine suffix pointing to the vineyard (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*, 1997; Blenkinsopp, AB 19, 2000).

notes.official: Verses 7–8 turn on measured judgment. The double rhetorical question of 27:7 — 'Has he struck him as he struck the one who struck him? Or was he slain as his slain were slain?' — leaves its pronouns unnamed, but the sense the commentators draw is that YHWH did not strike Israel with the severity he visited on Israel's oppressors (Wildberger; Kaiser, *Isaiah 13–39*, OTL). Verse 8 is among the hardest in the chapter: *bᵉsaʾsᵉʾāh* is a hapax, taken here from *sᵉʾāh* 'measure' ('in measure'; JPS 'In full measure') rather than from a root 'drive away'; *bᵉšallᵉḥāh* 'by sending her away' carries a possible divorce/exile register; and the text shifts from second person ('you contend with her') to third ('he removed her') mid-verse — a shift the translation preserves rather than normalizing. The 'harsh blast in the day of the east wind' (*rûaḥ qāšāh … yôm qāḏîm*) is the scorching sirocco.

i18n.en: Therefore by this the iniquity of Jacob shall be atoned for, and this is the full fruit of the removal of his sin: when he makes all the altar-stones like crushed chalkstones, no Asherim or sun-pillars shall stand.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן בְּזֹאת֙ יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְזֶ֕ה כָּל־פְּרִ֖י הָסִ֣ר חַטָּאת֑וֹ בְּשׂוּמ֣וֹ ׀ כָּל־אַבְנֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֗חַ כְּאַבְנֵי־גִר֙ מְנֻפָּצ֔וֹת לֹֽא־יָקֻ֥מוּ אֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְחַמָּנִֽים׃

notes.official: The measured judgment issues in atonement and cult-purge. *Yᵉḵuppar ʿăwōn-yaʿăqōḇ* 'the iniquity of Jacob shall be atoned for' pairs the *kpr* expiation-verb (overlay `kupar-atonement-isaiah`, now covering 27:9) with *ʿăwōn* 'iniquity' (central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`, extended to 27:9). The condition of that atonement is the demolition of the cult: the altar-stones ground 'like crushed chalkstones,' so that 'no *ʾăšērîm* or *ḥammānîm* shall stand.' The *ʾăšērîm* are the wooden poles of the goddess Asherah — the Hebrew reflex of Ugaritic *ʾAṯiratu*, ʾIlu's consort and mother of the gods (central `athirat-asherah-…`; deliberately not applied here, since 27:9 names the cult-object, not the goddess). *Ḥammānîm* are rendered 'sun-pillars' (NJPS 'incense-altars') (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp, AB 19).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י עִ֤יר בְּצוּרָה֙ בָּדָ֔ד נָוֶ֕ה מְשֻׁלָּ֥ח וְנֶעֱזָ֖ב כַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר שָׁ֣ם יִרְעֶ֥ה עֵ֛גֶל וְשָׁ֥ם יִרְבָּ֖ץ וְכִלָּ֥ה סְעִפֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: For the fortified city is solitary, a habitation forsaken and abandoned like the wilderness; there the calf shall graze, and there it shall lie down and consume its branches.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י עִ֤יר בְּצוּרָה֙ בָּדָ֔ד נָוֶ֕ה מְשֻׁלָּ֥ח וְנֶעֱזָ֖ב כַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר שָׁ֣ם יִרְעֶ֥ה עֵ֛גֶל וְשָׁ֥ם יִרְבָּ֖ץ וְכִלָּ֥ה סְעִפֶֽיהָ׃

paragraphs.text: בִּיבֹ֤שׁ קְצִירָהּ֙ תִּשָּׁבַ֔רְנָה נָשִׁ֕ים בָּא֖וֹת מְאִיר֣וֹת אוֹתָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עַם־בִּינוֹת֙ ה֔וּא עַל־כֵּן֙ לֹֽא־יְרַחֲמֶ֣נּוּ עֹשֵׂ֔הוּ וְיֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א יְחֻנֶּֽנּוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: When its harvest is dried up, they are broken off; women come and set them alight. For it is a people without understanding; therefore its Maker will not have compassion on it, and its Fashioner will not be gracious to it.
i18n.he: בִּיבֹ֤שׁ קְצִירָהּ֙ תִּשָּׁבַ֔רְנָה נָשִׁ֕ים בָּא֖וֹת מְאִיר֣וֹת אוֹתָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עַם־בִּינוֹת֙ ה֔וּא עַל־כֵּן֙ לֹֽא־יְרַחֲמֶ֣נּוּ עֹשֵׂ֔הוּ וְיֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א יְחֻנֶּֽנּוּ׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד־נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאַתֶּ֧ם תְּלֻקְּט֛וּ לְאַחַ֥ד אֶחָ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that YHWH will beat off the grain, from the flowing stream of the River to the Wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gathered up one by one, O children of Israel.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד־נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאַתֶּ֧ם תְּלֻקְּט֛וּ לְאַחַ֥ד אֶחָ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

notes.official: The chapter closes on ingathering. YHWH 'beats off the grain' (*yaḥbōṭ*, the verb for beating olives or grain from the stalk; the object 'grain' supplied, as JPS supplies '[His fruit]') 'from the flowing stream of the River' — the Euphrates — 'to the Wadi of Egypt' (Wadi el-ʿArish), the idealized north-south boundaries of the land, and the exiles are 'gathered up one by one' (*tᵉluqqᵉṭû lᵉ-ʾaḥaḏ ʾeḥāḏ*). *Šibbōleṯ* puns: 'flowing stream' here, but also 'ear of grain,' chiming with the threshing-verb (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp, AB 19).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִתָּקַע֮ בְּשׁוֹפָ֣ר גָּדוֹל֒ וּבָ֗אוּ הָאֹֽבְדִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְהַנִּדָּחִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֧וּ לַיהוָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that a great trumpet shall be blown, and those perishing in the land of Assyria and those driven out in the land of Egypt shall come, and they shall bow down to YHWH on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִתָּקַע֮ בְּשׁוֹפָ֣ר גָּדוֹל֒ וּבָ֗אוּ הָאֹֽבְדִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְהַנִּדָּחִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֧וּ לַיהוָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

notes.official: *Yittāqaʿ bᵉ-šôp̄ār gāḏôl* — 'a great trumpet shall be blown' — summons 'those perishing (*hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm*) in the land of Assyria and those driven out (*han-niddāḥîm*) in the land of Egypt' to bow down to YHWH on the holy mountain in Jerusalem: the eschatological ingathering of the lost and the outcast. *Šôp̄ār* is the ram's-horn (JPS 'horn'; the transliteration 'shofar' marks the cultic register). *Hištaḥăwû* 'they shall bow down' is here cultic worship of the deity — a different register from the human-homage 'made obeisance' of the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` entry (Genesis-scoped, deliberately not applied). The great-trumpet ingathering feeds the later gathering-of-the-dispersed tradition (cf. Matt 24:31; Wildberger; Blenkinsopp, AB 19).
